headline: Giant telescope in Chile turns for the first time

sources.title: Extremely Large Telescope reaches a major milestone | Space photo of the day for July 13, 2026

chunks.text: Engineers in Chile's Atacama Desert have {{pulled off}} something [[amazing]]. At the construction site of the Extremely Large Telescope, or ELT, they turned the giant telescope structure around its axis for the very first time. To get it moving, a small team first pushed the machine [[by hand]], just centimeters [[at a time]], while others {{looked on}}. After that, powerful motors {{took over}} and completed a full turn.

verbs.wrong: To manage to finish something at the very last moment
verbs.correct: To succeed in doing something difficult

verbs.wrong: To watch over something in order to keep it safe
verbs.correct: To watch something without taking part in it

verbs.wrong: To fill in for someone else for a short time
verbs.correct: To take control of something from someone else

chunks.text: The ELT is a huge machine, but it moves in a very gentle way. The whole structure is {{held up}} by a layer of oil only 80 microns thin, which lets it slide almost without any [[effort]]. When it is done, the telescope's main mirror will be {{made up of}} 798 segments of special glass. Together, they will {{carry out}} the work of one giant mirror, 39 meters wide.

verbs.wrong: To delay something or make it late
verbs.correct: To support the weight of something

verbs.wrong: To invent something that is not true
verbs.correct: To form the whole of something from smaller parts

verbs.wrong: To keep doing something without stopping
verbs.correct: To do or perform a task

chunks.text: The numbers behind the project are [[hard to imagine]]. Right now, the metal parts {{add up to}} about 3,500 metric tons. That weight will {{go up}} to more than 4,600 metric tons once the mirrors and science instruments are [[in place]]. Because the whole thing can turn, the telescope will be able to point at any area of the sky and study [[faraway]] galaxies.

verbs.wrong: To seem sensible or make sense
verbs.correct: To reach a certain total when combined

verbs.wrong: To rise above and pass a fixed limit
verbs.correct: To rise or become higher in amount

chunks.text: This test was an important [[milestone]] [[on the road to]] finishing the ELT. Builders expect to {{wrap up}} the work around 2028. When it opens, the telescope's [[enormous]] mirror will make it {{stand out}} as the largest optical telescope in the world. Many astronomers already {{look forward to}} the first clear images it will [[capture]].

vocab.def: To watch something without taking part in it
ex: A large crowd looked on as the parade passed by.
The children looked on while the magician did his trick.

vocab.def: To take control of something from someone else
ex: A new manager will take over the store next month.

vocab.def: To support the weight of something
ex: Four strong columns hold up the roof.

vocab.def: To form the whole of something from smaller parts
ex: Water is made up of hydrogen and oxygen.

vocab.def: To do or perform a task
ex: Doctors carried out several tests on the patient.

vocab.def: To reach a certain total when combined
ex: The bills added up to more than we expected.
All the small costs add up to a large sum.
Her savings added up to a few thousand dollars.

vocab.def: To rise or become higher in amount
ex: House prices went up again this year.
The temperature will go up tomorrow afternoon.
Ticket costs have gone up since last summer.
The workers wrapped up the project ahead of time.
Let us wrap up this meeting and go home.

vocab.def: To be clearly better or more noticeable than others
ex: Her bright red coat made her stand out in the crowd.
One student's essay really stood out from the rest.

vocab.def: To feel happy and excited about a future event
ex: I look forward to seeing you next week.
The kids look forward to summer vacation every year.
We are looking forward to the concert on Friday.
The view from the top of the mountain was amazing.
She did an amazing job on her final project.

wordDefs.def: Using your hands and not a machine
ex: My grandmother sews all her curtains by hand.
We washed the dishes by hand after the party.

wordDefs.def: In small amounts or steps, one after another
ex: He climbed the stairs two at a time.
I can only carry three boxes at a time.

wordDefs.def: The energy or work you use to do something
ex: It took a lot of effort to finish the race.
He made an effort to arrive on time.

wordDefs.def: Difficult to picture in your mind
ex: It is hard to imagine life without the internet.

wordDefs.def: Ready and in the correct position
ex: All the chairs are in place for the meeting.

He dreams of traveling to faraway places.

wordDefs.def: An important event in the progress of something
ex: Her first paycheck was a milestone in her life.
Walking again after the accident was a big milestone.
After the surgery, she is on the road to recovery.
Our team is on the road to the final game.
They live in an enormous house near the lake.

wordDefs.def: To catch or record something, such as an image
ex: I want to capture this moment in a photo.
The camera can capture very small details.

tf.s: Motors moved the whole telescope first, and then workers took over by hand.
tf.why: It was the other way around. Workers pushed it by hand first, and then the motors took over to finish the turn.

tf.s: The telescope's main mirror will be made up of 798 segments of special glass.
tf.why: The story says the main mirror will be made up of 798 glass segments.

tf.s: Engineers pulled off the first full rotation of the giant structure.
tf.why: The engineers pulled off the difficult job of turning the huge structure for the first time.

tf.s: The team decided to wrap up the whole telescope by 2026.
tf.why: Builders expect to wrap up the work around 2028, not 2026.

tf.s: The heavy structure is held up by a very thin layer of oil.
tf.why: The story says the structure is held up by a layer of oil only 80 microns thin.

tf.s: The telescope's main mirror will be made up of a single giant piece of glass.
tf.why: False. The mirror will be made up of 798 separate segments of special glass.
